feedback.problem:
Find the range of values of $k$ for which the series
${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{9}^{kn}}{{3}^{8n}}$
converges. Do not round the answer.

$k$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the series so that it's in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }a{r}^{n},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{9}^{kn}}{{3}^{8n}} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{(\frac{{9}^{k}}{{3}^{8}})}^{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{(\frac{{9}^{k}}{{9}^{4}})}^{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{({9}^{k-4})}^{n}\end{aligned}
$$

We see that this is a geometric series with a common ratio of $r={9}^{k-4}.$ 

For the series to converge, we require $|r|<1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|{9}^{k-4}| & <1 \\ {9}^{k-4} & <1.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we could remove the absolute value bars because ${9}^{k-4}$ is always positive.

The equation ${9}^{k-4}=1$ has the solution $k=4.$ Now, since ${9}^{k-4}$ increases as $k$ increases, the solution to ${9}^{k-4}<1$ must be $k<4.$
